title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 91
paragraphs: Then, as the stranger of Samos pressed his plea, Leotychides inquired — either wishing to hear for the sake of the omen, or perhaps by a chance Providence brought about: “Stranger of Samos, what is your name?” He said, “Hegesistratos.” Leotychides cut short the rest of the speech, stopping all that Hegesistratos had intended to say further, and said: “I accept the omen given in the name Hegesistratos, stranger of Samos. For your part, see that you give us assurances — you and the men with you — that the Samians will be our zealous allies without fail; and after that, sail away home.”
